finding.headers_extra.coop_missing: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy is missing or ineffective: the page is not isolated from other sites' windows.
headers_extra.coop_partial: Partial isolation: opened windows (popups) keep a link ({value})
headers_extra.corp_ok: Resource restricted to its origin or site ({value})
headers_extra.corp_open: Resource explicitly open to all origins ({value})
headers_extra.obsolete_expect_ct: Expect-CT is deprecated: browsers now enforce certificate transparency
headers_extra.obsolete_hpkp: HPKP was removed from browsers: delete it (risk of locking the site)
headers_extra.obsolete_legacy_csp: Pre-standard prefixed CSP header: ignored, use Content-Security-Policy
headers_extra.obsolete_xss: Browsers removed the XSS filter: drop the header or set it to 0
module.headers_extra.checks: Evaluates cross-origin isolation (COOP, COEP, CORP) and flags obsolete headers to remove (HPKP, Expect-CT, active X-XSS-Protection, Feature-Policy).
module.headers_extra.fix:
Remove the flagged obsolete headers where they are defined (web server, application, CDN): `Public-Key-Pins` (HPKP, it can lock visitors out of the site), `Expect-CT`, `Feature-Policy` (replaced by `Permissions-Policy`), `X-Webkit-CSP` and `X-Content-Security-Policy` (replaced by `Content-Security-Policy`). For `X-XSS-Protection`, delete it or set it to `0`.
Add `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` to isolate the page from other sites' windows (see the snippet). If the site opens third-party windows that must answer back (OAuth sign-in, payment in a separate window), use `same-origin-allow-popups` and test those flows.
Add `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin` (or `same-site`) so that other sites cannot load your resources. For a deliberately public resource (font, image served to partners, open API), use `cross-origin` on that path only.
Optional, test in staging first: `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` (or `credentialless`). Every third-party resource loaded by the page must then allow being loaded (CORP or CORS), otherwise the browser blocks it. This header mainly serves to get full origin isolation.
Check: `curl -sI https://example.com | grep -iE 'cross-origin|public-key-pins|expect-ct|feature-policy|x-xss'` must show only the isolation headers you want; also check the sign-in and payment pages in the browser, then run the scan again.
module.headers_extra.fix_snippet:
# nginx
add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin" always;
add_header Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy "same-origin" always;

# Apache
Header always set Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin"
Header always set Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy "same-origin"
Header always unset Public-Key-Pins
Header always unset Expect-CT
Header always unset Feature-Policy

# IIS
<system.webServer>
  <httpProtocol>
    <customHeaders>
      <add name="Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy" value="same-origin" />
      <add name="Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy" value="same-origin" />
      <remove name="Public-Key-Pins" />
      <remove name="Expect-CT" />
      <remove name="Feature-Policy" />
    </customHeaders>
  </httpProtocol>
</system.webServer>

# Caddy
example.com {
    header {
        Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin"
        Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy "same-origin"
        -Public-Key-Pins
        -Expect-CT
        -Feature-Policy
    }
}
module.headers_extra.title: Additional headers
module.headers_extra.why: COOP and COEP isolate the page from other sites (side-channel attacks, leaks between windows). An obsolete header has no effect, or is even dangerous: HPKP can lock visitors out of the site.
